Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the ShopSphere Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for queuing up will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Emily Carter, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to ShopSphere's Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; and Taylor Kim, COO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, CEO of ShopSphere.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Emily, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q2 performance, driven by robust seller performance metrics and impressive revenue growth both year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter. Our focus remains on accelerating new product and service launches that are already showing promising early traction and positive customer feedback. We are also committed to navigating logistics and shipping cost pressures from supply chain disruptions through targeted mitigation strategies.

We are excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our ShopNova Personalize engine, EcoThread sustainable apparel line, and ShopNova Express quick-commerce service, which we believe will significantly enhance customer engagement and marketplace take rates.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. Let's kick off the financial review by diving into our top-line performance, where we delivered another strong quarter of revenue growth, significantly outperforming our guidance across both year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter metrics. As a reminder, heading into this quarter, we guided for total revenue of $27.5 billion to $28.5 billion, implying YoY growth of 12% to 15% and QoQ growth of 6% to 9%. I'm thrilled to report that we came in at $28.7 billion, representing 14.8% YoY growth—smack in the upper half of our guidance range—and 9.2% QoQ growth from Q1's $26.3 billion, exceeding the high end by 20 basis points. This marks our eighth straight quarter of double-digit YoY top-line expansion, even amidst persistent macroeconomic headwinds like cooling consumer sentiment and elevated inflation in key markets.

To give you the full picture, let's break this down by key drivers and segments. Our core Marketplace business, which accounted for 68% of total revenue at $19.5 billion, saw 16.2% YoY growth, fueled by a robust 12% increase in Gross Merchandise Value, or GMV, to $185 billion. Our take rate expanded 45 basis points to 10.6%, thanks to higher-margin categories like electronics and beauty outperforming—similar to how we've seen surges in AI gadget demand. Active customers grew 8% YoY to 285 million globally, with order frequency up 4% and average order value, or AOV, steady at $52, reflecting sticky repeat purchases from our loyalty program.

Advertising revenue, our highest-margin segment at 22% of the mix and $6.3 billion, accelerated to 22.1% YoY growth, outpacing the broader digital ad market. Sponsored products and brand ads on our platform benefited from enhanced AI-powered recommendation engines, delivering 25% higher click-through rates year-over-year. We've rolled out the ShopSphere Ads Optimizer, a machine learning tool that's dynamically bidding across search, display, and offsite channels, tailored for e-commerce discovery.

Subscriptions and services rounded out at $2.9 billion, up 11.5% YoY, driven by our SpherePass membership base expanding to 152 million paid subscribers—a 10% increase—with penetration now at 53% of active customers. This segment's resilience comes with our fast-delivery perks, including same-day fulfillment in 85% of urban U.S. zip codes via expanded micro-fulfillment centers.

On the growth cadence, QoQ Marketplace GMV rose 7.5% sequentially, a step-up from Q1's 6.8%, as seasonal back-to-school demand kicked in early and our Prime Day equivalent event generated $14.2 billion in a single week—up 11% from last year. Advertising saw 10% QoQ acceleration due to advertiser budget shifts.

Regionally, North America remains our powerhouse at 62% of revenue, delivering 17.3% YoY growth to $17.8 billion, bolstered by market share gains in grocery and quick commerce—we've captured 28% U.S. online grocery share, chipping away at dominance through SphereFresh with 10-minute delivery in 15 major metros via robot couriers and logistics partnerships. APAC surged 25.4% YoY to $6.1 billion, led by India and Southeast Asia where GMV doubled in quick commerce, supercharged by localization like Hindi-language AI chat for product discovery. EMEA grew 8.7% to $4.8 billion, tempered by regulatory headwinds, but we're mitigating with compliant local storefronts and a 15% ramp in private-label assortments.

These results underscore the payoff from our Velocity 2025 initiative: $2.5 billion invested in cloud optimizations slashed data latency by 40%, enabling real-time personalization that boosted conversion rates 18%. We're leaning into GenAI for dynamic pricing—testing models that adjust AOV based on competitor signals—while expanding seller tools to 2.5 million third-party vendors, up 20% YoY. Amid softening discretionary spend, our focus on essentials and high-LTV categories positions us for sustained 12-15% long-term revenue CAGR. We not only met but exceeded our Q2 guidance through operational excellence and category tailwinds, setting a solid foundation for H2.

Turning now to our seller performance metrics, which remain a cornerstone of our marketplace vitality here at ShopSphere. Our third-party sellers drive over 65% of our GMV, making these KPIs critical for top-line growth and ecosystem sustainability. Active sellers are defined as those generating at least $1,000 in trailing 12-month GMV, and I'll cover average revenue per seller, or ARPU, with trends, regional dynamics, and strategic levers.

We ended Q2 with 2.8 million active sellers globally, up 28% year-over-year and 7% quarter-over-quarter. This marks our strongest quarterly seller growth since Q1 2022, surpassing the post-pandemic onboarding surge. For the full fiscal year to date, we've added over 650,000 net new active sellers, bringing our total cohort to a record high. New seller activations hit 450,000 in the quarter alone, fueled by our revamped Seller Onboarding Portal, which reduced time-to-first-sale from 14 days to just 4 days via automated KYC verification and AI-powered product listing suggestions.

Retention remains robust at 92% for sellers with over 12 months tenure, compared to industry benchmarks around 85% for platforms like Etsy or eBay. This stems from our Seller Success Dashboard, rolled out in beta last quarter and now at 40% adoption, using predictive analytics to flag at-risk sellers and recommend personalized interventions like inventory optimization or ad spend adjustments. We've seen a 15% uplift in retention among dashboard users.

Average annual ARPU climbed to $48,200, a healthy 18% increase YoY and 5% QoQ. This outpaces GMV growth, reflecting our focus on seller monetization without compromising marketplace breadth. ARPU from fulfillment services—like our ShopSphere Fulfillment Network, or SFN—jumped 22% to $12,400 per seller, driven by Prime-eligible inventory mandates that boosted conversion rates by 14%. Advertising ARPU, via sponsored products and brand stores, rose 25% to $9,800, as sellers leaned into our GenAI-powered bidding engine, optimizing for ROAS in real-time and delivering a 2.3x average return.

High-ticket categories like consumer electronics and home & garden led, with ARPU exceeding $75,000—up 12% YoY—thanks to our expanded B2B wholesale portal, now live in 12 countries. Fashion and beauty sellers, 35% of our base, saw 8% ARPU growth, but we're addressing this with localized trend forecasting tools integrated with data from Nielsen and SimilarWeb.

Regionally, North America, 42% of active sellers at 1.18 million, delivered 12% YoY growth with the highest ARPU at $62,500—bolstered by mature adoption of premium tiers like our Enterprise Seller Program, where top 1% sellers average $450K annually. APAC exploded with 45% seller growth to 850,000 actives, led by India and Southeast Asia, where ARPU hit $32,100 amid booming smartphone penetration and partnerships with local wallets like Paytm and GCash. Vernacular-language seller tools and micro-fulfillment centers in Tier-2 cities drove a 30% ARPU ramp. Europe grew 22% to 520,000 sellers, with ARPU at $51,200, though regulatory headwinds like the DSA are prompting investments in compliance automation. Emerging markets like LATAM and MENA added 18% growth to 250,000 combined, with ARPU scaling from $18,000 via cross-border export programs tapping U.S. demand.

These metrics underscore our Seller-First Flywheel: more actives beget better selection, driving buyer traffic and higher ARPU. We're doubling down with $250 million in FY24 capex for seller tech, including full rollout of our ML-driven Dynamic Pricing Suite—already boosting seller margins 11% in pilots—and integration with ERP giants like SAP and Oracle for seamless inventory sync. Our Green Seller Certification, held by 15% of actives, correlates with 20% higher ARPU from eco-conscious Prime shoppers.

Looking ahead, we guide for 25-30% active seller growth and 15-20% ARPU expansion in FY24, assuming no major macro shocks. This positions us to capture share from fragmented players while fending off hyperscalers.

Gross margin was 38.2%, impacted by logistics and shipping costs amid supply chain disruptions, which compressed margins by 210 basis points YoY. In our e-commerce space, logistics is the backbone of our customer promise, driving net promoter scores through reliable delivery and fueling our 28% YoY GMV growth to $4.2 billion this quarter. But persistent disruptions have pressured this line. Global issues—from Red Sea tensions, Panama Canal constraints, U.S. West Coast port congestion, and avian flu effects on air freight—spiked ocean freight rates 145% YoY per the Shanghai Containerized Freight Index, hitting 4,200 points in June. Our core sourcing from Asia-Pacific, 62% of SKUs, saw container spot rates from Shanghai to Los Angeles surge to $5,800 per FEU from $2,400. Air freight for high-AOV items jumped 35% to $4.20 per kg.

This translated to total logistics and shipping costs rising 32% YoY to $428 million, or 10.2% of GMV—up from 7.8% and above our 8-9% target. Fulfillment costs ballooned 41% to $285 million, driven by 22% higher dwell times at ports like Ningbo and Busan, averaging 7.2 days versus 3. Outbound shipping added 18% inflation due to surcharges amid softening volumes.

In North America, 55% of GMV, port strikes added 10-14 days to lead times, forcing pivots to West Coast routes despite Panama limits, hitting apparel hardest with lead times to 65 days and inventory turns dropping to 6.9x. EMEA, 28% of GMV, saw Red Sea reroutings inflate rates 220%, pushing UK costs up 28% and dipping conversions 5%. APAC grew better with localized sourcing but still 19% cost growth.

We've clawed back 40% of pressure proactively. Our AI-powered logistics orchestration with Flexport and FourKites optimized 68% of ocean bookings, shaving 12% off freight and reducing stockouts 22%. We've nearshored 18% of apparel to Mexico and Turkey, targeting 25% ocean reduction by FY25. Micro-fulfillment centers—42 sites with robotic picking—enable same-day for 45% of nearby orders, compressing last-mile from $12.45 to $9.87, a 21% savings. Predictive analytics pre-positioned buffer stock, mitigating $55 million shortfalls. Volume commitments yielded 7% rebates, and drone pilots trim 30% on rural lanes.

Reverse logistics saw returns up to 15%, but AI disposition routes 62% to resale, recovering $28 million. We've hedged 65% of H2 ocean contracts and are investing $250 million in owned hubs and EV fleets for 18% ROI by FY26. Blockchain for traceability cuts fraud 14%.

For Q3, we expect costs at 9.8-10.3% of GMV, moderating to 18% YoY growth. Full-year guide $1.72-1.78 billion, implying 150 bps margin expansion in H2. Our 95% on-time rate positions us resiliently.

Today, I'd also like to dive into our new product and service launches, contributing over 18% to our total GMV of $2.8 billion—up 22% YoY. We're thrilled with early traction on ShopNova Personalize, our AI recommendation engine; EcoThread sustainable apparel; and ShopNova Express quick-commerce.

ShopNova Personalize, trained on 500 million interactions, is live for 65% of users. Conversion rates jumped 28% in tests, uplifting AOV 15% to $145, with GMV at $420 million or 15% of revenue. App ratings to 4.7/5, NPS up 12 to 68, with 72% citing it for repeats. Edge computing keeps latency under 50ms for mobile Gen Z. US leads at 32% lift, EU at 22%. We're expanding to APAC with $25 million.

EcoThread, 250 SKUs from recycled materials, hit $85 million GMV—40% ahead—65% sell-through, 42% margins via Dhaka center. Reviews 4.6/5, 85% positive sentiment. North America 55% of sales, 38% repeats. Plans for 1,000 SKUs.

ShopNova Express in five US metros and two EU cities achieved 28% penetration, 14-minute deliveries, $150 million GMV, NPS 72. Investing $40 million for more hubs, eyeing profitability Q1 2025.

These have grown active customers to 45 million (+19% YoY), take rate to 22.5%, LTV up 14%. They fortify our 12-15% FY24 growth guidance.

Operating expenses were $10.2 billion, representing 35.6% of revenue. Our net income for the quarter was $2.1 billion, or $1.65 per share. We ended the quarter with $45 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance of revenue $115-118 billion, adjusted EBITDA margins of 18-20%, and active customer growth of 12-15%.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question and answer session. [Operator instructions for Q&A session]. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith:
Thanks for taking my question. Alex, your seller metrics look impressive, especially the 28% YoY active seller growth and ARPU expansion. Can you talk about the sustainability of this in a tougher macro environment, and any risks to retention?

Alex Rivera:
Great question, John. Sustainability comes down to our Seller-First Flywheel, which we've emphasized. The 92% retention for mature sellers is driven by tools like the Seller Success Dashboard, delivering real 15% uplifts. In a tougher macro, we're seeing balanced regional growth—APAC's 45% surge offsets any NA slowdowns—and premium programs for top sellers keep ARPU resilient. Risks like regulation are real, but our $250 million capex in seller tech, including Dynamic Pricing, mitigates them. We're confident in 25-30% growth guidance.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Wong:
Jordan, on logistics, those supply chain disruptions sound painful with 32% cost growth. What's your outlook for H2 normalization, and how much more margin expansion can we expect from mitigations like nearshoring and AI orchestration?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Lisa. We've already clawed back 40% of the pressure, and H2 should see moderation to 18% YoY growth as Red Sea stabilizes and efficiencies ramp. Nearshoring 18% of production cuts ocean dependency toward 25% reduction by FY25, while micro-fulfillment and AI rerouting deliver 21% last-mile savings. With hedges in place and capex for autonomy, we're guiding 150 bps expansion in H2, positioning margins toward our long-term target despite risks like geopolitics.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Thompson with JPMorgan.

Mike Thompson:
Taylor, congrats on the new launches—ShopNova Personalize and Express sound sticky. What's the customer feedback loop telling you, and how do you plan to scale these profitably amid competition from Temu and DoorDash?

Taylor Kim:
Appreciate it, Mike. Feedback is strong: 4.7/5 ratings for Personalize, 72 NPS for Express, driving 28% conversions and 52% weekly retention. We're scaling Personalize to APAC Q4 with proven 3x LTV uplift, EcoThread to 1,000 SKUs on 42% margins, and Express to 10 more hubs at $2.50 unit economics. Profitability by Q1 2025, countering competitors via omnichannel speed and personalization we own end-to-end.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
